title: _safePay revert in stake()/unstake() blocks principal adjustments during transient shortfall

classification.assetImpact: UX regression. No direct loss: principal remains owned; pending reward remains accrued and claimable when balance recovers. emergencyWithdraw is an escape but is disproportionate (forfeits all pending).
attackPath: 1. User has principal staked with non-zero pending.
2. Contract rewardToken balance temporarily drops below the user's pending (another claimer just drained it, or dispatcher lag).
3. User calls stake/unstake; _safePay reverts the entire tx.
4. User can wait (pending remains) or call emergencyWithdraw (forfeits all pending).
classification.likelihood: low - transient shortfall windows are short; pending is preserved across the wait.
classification.assumptions: Contract is in a transient shortfall state. No value is lost if the user waits.
classification.externalRequirements: Shortfall condition caused by dispatcher lag or timing with another claim.

justification: Low/QA. This is a UX trade-off from story-002's revert-on-shortfall change - the fix for the prior silent-forfeiture Medium necessarily means reverts happen under shortfall. Users do not lose funds: pending reward is preserved in storage and claimable once the pool is replenished. emergencyWithdraw exists as an escape. Does not rise to Medium (no protocol function broken, no value leak) - the described failure mode is a predictable consequence of the prior fix and is correctable via a rollover semantic in future work.
